showing or saying that you are sorry that something has happened
Example:  I am the one who's supposed to be apologetic.
These are words you use to describe someone.
doing things carefully, using an ordered system
Example: I am usually a very methodical person.
Example: I think I got carried away.
feeling guilty about something that you cannot think about anything else
Example: I know I wasn't supposed to do that, but I was plagued by guilt.
Example: I didn't mean to sound opportunistic.
deceiving people in order to get what you want
Example: That was a sly move!
doing things only because they will give you an advantage that other people do not have
Example: I am not the self-seeking type and you know that.
Be Supposed to and Was/Were Supposed to
You use be supposed to and was going to to explain how things were done.

You use the structure be supposed to when you want to talk about expectations, obligations or arrangements. You can use this structure using the Past tense to talk about things that you were obligated to do, but didn't or couldn't do.

The structure is:

Subject + To be + supposed to + verb

I was supposed to be there yesterday, but my flight was canceled.

**Pronunciation tip**:
When you say be supposed to, you link the /d/ and /t/ sounds together.

Like this:
Be suppose_to

You use the structure was going to when you want to talk about things that you had planned or intended to do.

The structure is:

was/were + going to + verb

I was going to go to the shoemaker to get it fixed.
I know we were supposed to meet earlier, but I got stuck in a meeting. I was going to text you, but ended up forgetting - sorry!
We were supposed to use our notes to do that.
I was going to tell you earlier, but I didn't have the courage to.

In a work environment there may come a time when you have to talk about an event that doesn't commonly happen. You can use different phrases to express that is it an unusual event. Look at the chart below. It contains a list of phrases or expressions you can use.
